bullets.title: AI infrastructure selloff deepens: record HF de-grossing, semis -7% worst day since June
bullets.body: The week was defined by violent AI/hyperscaler unwind—GS TMT L/S Broad AI Basket -4.1%, TMT Mo' Basket -7.8%, SOX -3.2% on the week with one day down 6.8% (worst since June). GS Risk Appetite Indicator hit lowest since April; ~$20bn TMT net selling over 2 weeks approached July episode levels. Hedge fund L/S alpha fell -2.9% MTD (worst since Feb 2021), TMT-focused funds down 9.6% MTD; gross leverage at 312%, net at 71.8% (3rd percentile 1-year). Long sales outpaced short covers 3.4-to-1; single stocks net sold 6th straight week. Retail buying at slowest pace in a year.

bullets.title: META capex scrutiny triggers record 119bp CDS; equity raise of $40B+ expected early 2027
bullets.body: META beat Q3 with revenue +26% YoY and strong Muse metrics (10M users, 25% DAU, $200+ avg purchase), but 5-year CDS hit all-time high at 114-119bp as the company disclosed 'hundreds of billions' in AI financing needs and guided FY26 capex to $135-145B. Management deferred 2027 capex guidance to Q4, announced Class C non-voting shares effective Jan 19 2027 (enabling capital raises without diluting Zuckerberg's control), and confirmed FCF turned negative (-$2.1B in Q3). FCF estimated at -$95B in 2027. Berkshire cited as potential anchor for a $40B+ equity raise expected within weeks.

bullets.title: AI capex ROI debate escalates; credit markets stopping funding weakest players, hyperscaler CDS at wides
bullets.body: Multiple sell-side teams flagged the growing gap between AI capex commitments and revenue visibility as the dominant market theme. CoreWeave's 2031 notes yielded ~16% and unsecured bonds widened ~300bp since August; ORCL CDS at widest levels. Anthropic S-1 expected ~Oct 26 with IPO by Thanksgiving; valuation floor ~$1.5T (down from $2T+). Jefferies argued AI capex will grow from $1.3T in 2027 to $2.5T by 2030 and the infrastructure glut (like 1990s fiber) ultimately expands adoption. 22V noted 2027 capex plans remain high-conviction; 2028+ viability questioned. CRWV needs $24-37B additional debt to reach 3.3GW by YE27.

bullets.title: Rotation from AI/Semis to Software, Value, and Defensives accelerating; SPX ex-AI now outperforming
bullets.body: OpCo downgraded semis to Market Weight after 18-month advance broke 200-day MA (participation collapsed from 88% to 26%); upgraded Software/Commercial Services/Insurance to OW. Software (IGV) +5.73% vs SOX -2.72% on the week. S&P ex-AI index now outperforming S&P 500 YTD; equal-weight outperformed cap-weight by ~160bp WTD. Small caps (Russell 2000) +2% vs Nasdaq -0.71%; Value and Profitability factors leading. SPX support at 7,600/7,500/7,300; breadth critical test—RTY broke below 200-day, Russell 3000 participation below 50%; 60% threshold is recovery hurdle.

bullets.title: SpaceX confirms 2.5-3GW compute target by YE26, 10GW+ in 2027; tower stocks surge on wireless entry plans
bullets.body: SpaceX Q3 revenue beat at $14.6B (+161% YoY); Super Intelligence segment turned profitable for first time ($7.6B revenue). Company raised compute guidance to 2.5-3GW by YE26 with 10GW incremental in 2027, targeting $500B-$1T ARR exit by YE27. Separately, SpaceX confirmed discussions with Crown Castle and other tower REITs to access 80,000 US cell sites for a fourth national wireless carrier buildout—tower stocks (CCI, SBAC, AMT) surged 8-10% while AT&T and Verizon fell 5-6%. SpaceX acquired Grain's 800MHz spectrum; hybrid satellite-terrestrial launch targeted ~2 years.

bullets.title: FOMC next week expected to hold; December hike at 87-88% odds; Fed recognizes AI boom as inflationary
bullets.body: Across JPM, Piper, and 22V, consensus is Fed holds at Oct 28 meeting (90%+ probability) with a December hike increasingly priced (87-88% odds per futures). JPM forecasts additional hikes in Sept-Dec-Mar for 75bp total; Piper models 2 more hikes. Global headline CPI forecast at 4% ar and core at 3% ar—materially higher than 3 months ago, driven by oil up ~30% from last quarter's average. Fed described as recognizing AI investment boom as inflationary. ECB pause next week; December hike seen as near-certain; BoC starting hiking cycle.

bullets.title: WTI above $100/bbl on US-Iran escalation; Brent $20 above JPM fair value; oil technical target $120
bullets.body: WTI settled above $100/bbl for the first time this cycle, up 4.3% on the week (third straight weekly gain) on reports of US-Iran military planning post-midterms. Brent approached $116/bbl—JPM estimated Brent fair value at $94, implying a $20 geopolitical risk premium. 22V has technical target of $120 for oil, consistent with 2022 resistance. Energy sector +2.51% on the week vs consumer staples -1.83%. October flash manufacturing PMI's selling prices rose at fastest pace since August 2022. Iran-US diplomacy active through Qatar/Pakistan but unresolved on sequencing.

bullets.title: US midterms: Democrats 88-91% to take House, 60-65% Senate; debt ceiling dominates lame-duck agenda
bullets.body: 22V and Citi pegged Democrats at 88% odds for House and 60-65% Senate, with ~60% odds of unitary Democratic control. Lame-duck agenda dominated by Dec 11 government funding deadline and debt ceiling. Bipartisan permitting reform (BAAJA) at 50/50 odds in lame duck. Texas governor's race seen as the biggest data center policy risk—TCEQ closed permit portal; Polymarket had Abbott at 78%. Democratic control expected to increase META/AI oversight, data center restrictions scrutiny, and SpaceX contract review.

bullets.title: S&P 500 Q3 earnings: 83% beat rate, EPS growth 29.5%—but surprise magnitude far below historical norms
bullets.body: With 24% of S&P 500 market cap reported, blended Q3 EPS growth stands at 29.5% (near 29.6% expected), revenue growth at 12.7%. 83% beat rate exceeds 82% one-year and 78% five-year averages, but the aggregate EPS beat of 2.1% is far below the 13.8% one-year and 7.5% five-year norms. Sales beat rate (66%) is below both historical benchmarks. 80% of US companies beating EPS per MS data but magnitude of rewards more modest than historical. 35% of SPY/QQQ market cap due to report next week (MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN).

bullets.title: French sovereign crisis: OAT-Bund spread near 180bp, 10-year at 5% (24-year high); France most stressed EU market
bullets.body: French 10-year OAT yield crossed 5% for first time since 2002; France CDS spreads +247% in 2026 at GFC-era levels; OAT-Bund spread near 180bp. French REIT index corrected -18% since July peak; Bloomberg France REIT index at risk of further declines. ECB viewed French government as responsible for calming markets through fiscal commitment; TPI activation seen as very unlikely. JPM cut Q4 French GDP forecast to 1.0% ar (from 1.25%) due to social unrest. France most stressed European market per 22V.

bullets.title: US consumer resilient but confidence dipping; housing at cycle lows; freight costs squeezing margins
bullets.body: PSC Consumer Confidence Survey down 1.7pt to 98.4; record 59% of consumers say high prices eroding finances. NAHB Housing Market Index fell to 29 in October (lowest since 2012); September pending home sales -7.3% to record low; housing starts -5.2%. PulteGroup missed on closings/orders. P&G flagged $1.4B energy/commodity headwind. TSA throughput -2.5% y/y. October flash PMI services 57.9 and manufacturing 56.0 (both near-consensus), but selling prices rose at fastest pace since August 2022.

bullets.title: WDC delivers 55% revenue growth, 80%+ incremental margins; HDD supply constrained through 2031
bullets.body: Western Digital beat F1Q27 (revenue $4.38B, +5.8% above consensus; EPS $4.64, +12.9% above; GM 58.1%, +240bp above) and guided F2Q well above consensus ($5.1B revenue vs $4.57B, $5.80 EPS vs $4.82, GM 60-61%). Management cited demand visibility from top-7 customers through CY31; HAMR qualification Q1 2027, volume shipments H1 2027. 100% of FCF returned to shareholders; dividend raised 17%. Stock fell despite results amid sector rotation.

bullets.title: TXN blowout: GM 64.2% vs 61.1% expected; industrial, auto, data center all accelerating; 2027 pricing power building
bullets.body: TI reported Sep-Q revenue $6.06B (+2% beat), EPS $2.62 (+7.4% beat), and GM 64.2% vs 61.2% consensus—the widest outperformance on margins. Dec-Q guided $5.80-6.30B (midpoint +5% above street) with above-seasonal growth from Industrial, Auto, and Data Center. Management signaling 2027 pricing discussions underway as analog supply tightens; TXN has cleanroom capacity advantage. Data center growing near 100% YoY and now meaningful share of revenue. Prior GM peak was 69-70% at $4.9-5.2B quarterly revenue, suggesting significant upside.

bullets.title: SMCI pre-announced F1Q27 revenue $18.5-19.5B vs $14.5-15.5B guidance; GM recovering to 12-12.5%
bullets.body: Super Micro positively pre-announced fiscal Q1 2027 revenue guidance raised 27% above midpoint to $18.5-19.5B, with gross margins recovering to 12.0-12.5% vs 10.4-10.8% guidance. Management cited 'increased demand for AI platforms' and better enterprise customer mix. DELL and HPE rallied 6-7% in sympathy. This was cited as one of several constructive data points for AI infrastructure demand offsetting broader AI capex sentiment concerns.

bullets.title: Bloom Energy beats/raises third consecutive quarter; $5.8B supplier commitments signal scaling
bullets.body: BE reported Q3 beat and raised FY26 guidance +11% revenue, +17% operating income, +20% EPS for the third consecutive quarter. Backlog growth exceeded revenue growth; capacity expanding with $231M YTD capex (~4x FY25) and Fremont site addition. Morgan Stanley raised PT to $335 (from $310); OPCO and Citi also constructive. Stock sold off -12.7% on the week amid broader AI infrastructure rotation despite strong fundamentals; negative FCF and capacity expansion pace flagged by bears.

bullets.title: NFLX -6.6% on week: Q4 guide light, ad revenue cut to $2.7B from $3B, CCO and film chief replaced
bullets.body: Netflix Q3 beat consensus but guided Q4 revenue $13.44B (-0.6% vs consensus) with operating margin 26% including ~120bp headcount reduction impact. FY26 ad revenue guidance cut to $2.7B from ~$3B due to slower third-party integration rollout. Management replaced CCO Bela Bajaria (Peter Rice named successor) and dismissed film chief Dan Lin. Wolfe downgraded to peer perform. MS cut PT to $77 (17x FY28 EPS). Bears now focus on 2027 revenue guide risk of sub-10% growth.

bullets.title: Regional banks solid; KRE broke above 200/150-day MAs; AOCI marks reversing on 10-year move from 530 to 509bp
bullets.body: 22V noted regional bank quarters were solid; capital markets revenue slightly weaker on margin as expected; AOCI marks reversed given 10-year move from 530 to 509bp. Banks reinvesting maturing loans and securities at 125bp roll-up pickup (vs 100bp expected) and adding receive-fixed swaps. KRE broke above 200- and 150-day moving averages. Banks pushing back on agentic AI disruption narrative citing liability and cybersecurity risks. AXP beat on EPS ($4.68 vs $4.50) driven by provision, but revenue missed; billed business decelerated; 4Q guide implies ~$4.26 EPS below consensus.

bullets.title: Salesforce acquires Braze for $5.66B (58% premium); CRM stock -3% on organic growth concerns
bullets.body: Salesforce signed definitive agreement to acquire Braze for $47.50/share (~$5.66B EV, ~5x CY27 revenue). Deal funds from cash (~4 months of FY27 FCF), no debt financing. Close expected in Salesforce FY28; no FY27 guidance change. Strategic rationale: adds real-time mobile engagement and conversational marketing to Marketing Cloud. Antitrust risk flagged as Braze lists Salesforce/Adobe as competitors. Early investor feedback mixed-to-negative on organic growth and acquisition pace.

bullets.title: SPOT Q3 beat and raise; opex growth peaking; AI Remix and audiobook expansion seen as 2027 margin catalysts
bullets.body: Spotify Q3: premium subs +6M (beat +5M guide), GM 33.0% (beat 32.9% guidance), operating income €672M in-line, FCF €735M. Q4 guided with 10M net adds, GM 33.8%, OI €820M vs €808M consensus. Management expects opex growth to moderate from ~16% to ~8% in FY27 as AI investments shift to monetization. MS raised PT to $700; JPM to $700; KeyBanc to $690. Ad revenue tracking double-digit growth into H2. Stock +8-11% on results.

bullets.title: PHP vulnerability affects 70% of global websites; cyber names NET/FSLY rally; AI-generated attack costs near $0
bullets.body: AI tools independently discovered one of the most severe PHP vulnerabilities on record, enabling remote code execution on affected servers (70% of global web runs PHP). CVE discovery volumes running 290/day YTD, more than 2x 2025 levels. Citi noted NET and FSLY as primary edge/CDN beneficiaries of elevated patching urgency. MS stated 80-90% of cybersecurity attacks now AI-generated with attack costs trending toward $0. Major US banks detected unauthorized AI agents operating in customer accounts.
